source.title: Interim Rezoning Policy for Social Housing, Seniors Housing, and Institutional, Cultural and Recreational Uses in Former Community Vision Areas (approved 1 Nov 2023, amended 31 Mar 2026)
source.section: s.3.1.1; staff benchmark from the 998 E 19th Ave referral report
source.verify: Map 1 of the policy decides whether a site is inside a former Community Vision area; outside it the Affordable Housing Policies (1989) apply.

results.finding: Eligible for consideration as 100% social housing under the policy; height 22.3 m is above the staff benchmark of 19.9 to 21.3 m. The policy sets no maximum, so the number is negotiated with staff.
results.action: Manager and architect: expect staff to test the scheme against the RM-4 benchmark; prepare the shadow and daylight case.

results.title: Development cost levy and community amenity contribution treatment of social housing

source.title: 998 E 19th Ave referral report: CAC exempt under the policy's social housing exemption; DCL exempt as church and social housing (estimated value $3,075,715 at 30 Sep 2023 rates)
source.verify: Current DCL rates and exemptions: City of Vancouver DCL bulletin (not yet opened in this project).

results.title: Family-unit requirement in rezonings

source.title: City of Vancouver, Housing options for families: at least 35% two-bedroom-plus units including at least 5% three-bedroom-plus in rezonings; City-wide Design and Development Guidelines replace the 1992 guidelines

results.layer_title: City of Vancouver policies that attach to a rezoning
results.title: Social housing definition (Zoning and Development By-law s.2; DCL By-law 9755)

source.title: 998 E 19th Ave referral report: social housing as defined in the Vancouver Development Cost Levy By-law No. 9755 (at least 30% of units for households below the Housing Income Limits, rents not exceeding 30% of income, owned by a non-profit or government, secured by housing agreement for the longer of 60 years and the life of the building)
source.section: Tenure and affordability; Housing Agreement and Section 219 covenant

results.finding: Meets the City's social housing definition: 30.0% of units for households below HILs (minimum 30.0%), owned by a non profit society, secured for 60 years.

results.layer_title: City of Vancouver policies that attach to a rezoning
results.title: Protection of Trees By-law 9958: minimum trees, protection distances, cash in lieu

source.title: City of Vancouver Protection of Trees By-law No. 9958 (consolidated)
source.section: Schedule A (s.1.2), Schedule C (ss.5.1, 5.2, 6.2), s.6.2 cash in lieu, s.6.5 siting, s.7.2 arborist report

results.finding: Schedule C requires 20 trees on 2,811 m²; the option keeps 1 of 9 and plants 16, leaving 17, a shortfall of 3: plant 3 more at the by-law setbacks or pay $3,000 cash in lieu; the final count is set at the development permit.

values.survey_scope: every tree on the site, within 2 m of the boundary, and on the adjoining street

results.action: Architect: find room for the missing trees (1 m from side lines, 1.5 m from the building, 2.5 m apart) or budget the cash in lieu.

source.title: Province of BC, BC Building Code 2024; City of Vancouver, Guide to 2025 Vancouver Building By-law updates
source.section: Part 3 vs Part 9 basis (Div A 1.3.3.2); encapsulated mass timber
